fields.title: 📖 Imām aš-Šāfiʿī: monks are not killed deliberately
fields.body:
🖋️ **Imām aš-Šāfiʿī** said in meaning:

> ***The monks in monasteries, hermitages, and remote places are not killed deliberately; everyone who devotes himself to monasticism is left aside from being killed — as a following of Abū Bakr aṣ-Ṣiddīq, not merely as one’s own analogy.***

This shows an important standard in Siyar-Fiqh: not every person in enemy territory is treated the same. There are legal limits, transmitted practice, and precise distinction.

🌙 **Conclusion:** The Fiqh of Ahlus-Sunnah is bound to the Qurʾān, the Sunnah, and the practice of the Ṣaḥābah. Even in the law of war, limits remain — not anger, chaos, or indiscriminate killing.

immutable.source: 📝 aš-Šāfiʿī, al-Umm, Masāʾil fī al-Jihād wa’l-Jizya, Kitāb al-Ḥukm fī Qitāl al-Mushrikīn wa Masʾalat Māl al-Ḥarbī, Teil 4, S. 253–254.
